title: TypeScript: which security bugs does the compiler not catch?
short: Parse every input with a runtime schema, make `any` a lint error and check authorization in each handler, not only in middleware.
answer: Before your next release, parse every untrusted input with a runtime schema, make typescript-eslint's type-aware `no-unsafe-*` rules errors and check authorization in each handler, not only in middleware. Judge everything else by whether outside data can reach a shell, a query, a file path, a URL, an object merge, `eval` or raw HTML unchecked.
audience: Developers and tech leads writing production TypeScript for Node.js servers and React front ends, and the security people who review it

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Parse every input at runtime.
items.text: The compiler erases types and `as` casts[^tseveryday], and `JSON.parse()` and `.json()` return `any`[^tseany]. Parse bodies, params, headers and messages with a schema such as Zod's `z.strictObject()`, which rejects unknown keys[^zod].

items.title: Make the compiler and linter refuse `any`.
items.text: Keep `strict`, the default since TypeScript 6.0[^ts6], add `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`[^tsconfig] and lint with typescript-eslint's `strictTypeChecked`[^tsestrict]. Run `tsc --noEmit` in CI, because Node.js runs `.ts` files unchecked[^nodets].

items.title: Authorize where the data is read.
items.text: CVE-2025-29927 let attackers bypass authorization in Next.js middleware[^nextmw], and five more bypasses followed in 2026[^nextadv]. Check the user's right to each record in every handler and Server Action[^nextsec].

items.title: Keep input away from shells, SQL, `eval` and raw HTML.
items.text: Cross-site scripting, SQL injection, OS command injection and code injection rank 1st, 2nd, 9th and 10th in the 2025 CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Use parameterized queries and `execFile` with an argument array, never `eval` input, and render user text as JSX children.

items.title: Patch the framework within days.
items.text: CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell), an unauthenticated remote code execution bug in React Server Components rated CVSS 10, was disclosed on 3 December 2025[^react2shell]. CISA listed it as exploited two days later and now flags known ransomware use[^kev]. Patch within the patching sheet's deadlines and run Node.js 22, 24 or 26[^noderel].

items.title: Where does outside data enter?
items.text: Find the handlers, Server Actions, webhooks and queue consumers the change touches, including Next.js folders in brackets[^nextsec], and check that each parses its input first.

items.title: Did it add `any`, `as`, `!` or `@ts-expect-error`?
items.text: Ask why for each one near outside data, then follow that data to the sinks in the traps below.

items.title: Who may do this, to which record?
items.text: Missing authorization ranks 4th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Check ownership of the record, not just the login. Server Actions can be called with a direct POST, not just from your UI, so each one checks for itself[^nextsec].

items.title: Does it run code it didn't write?
items.text: Neither `vm`[^nodevm] nor the Permission Model is a sandbox: the model is a seat belt for trusted code[^nodeperm], and October's release closed two more gaps in it[^nodeoct]. Run untrusted code in its own container without secrets.

items.title: What leaves the server?
items.text: Return only the fields the client needs, and keep secrets out of `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables, which reach the browser[^nextsec]. Send new dependencies through the supply-chain sheet's checks.

blocks.title: TypeScript traps and what to use instead
items: **`JSON.parse(body) as Order`.** The cast checks nothing, so a missing field or a wrong type flows on[^tseveryday]. Use `Order.parse(JSON.parse(body))` and treat `as` on outside data as a bug.

**`exec("convert " + file)`.** `exec` runs a shell, and Node.js says never to pass it unsanitized input[^nodechild]. Use `execFile("convert", [file])`, or `spawn` without `shell: true`, and reject a `file` that starts with `-`. A React Native CLI command injection is on CISA's exploited list[^kev].

**`merge(target, req.body)` and `obj[a][b] = value`.** `__proto__` or `constructor.prototype` keys in input can add properties to every object in the process. oRPC's deserializer polluted the prototype before Zod validation ran (CVE-2026-28794, critical)[^orpc]. Use a `Map` or `Object.create(null)`[^owasppp], and make merge code skip those keys.

**`path.join(root, req.query.name)`.** Path traversal ranks 6th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Resolve the path with `path.resolve` or `fs.realpath` and reject it unless it starts with the root folder plus `path.sep`.

**`fetch(req.body.webhookUrl)`.** It can reach internal services and the cloud metadata address `169.254.169.254`. Allowlist hosts, validate the IP address you connect to and disable redirects[^owaspssrf] with `redirect: "error"`. WHATWG URL rules read `0127.0.0.1` as `87.0.0.1`, some OS resolvers as `127.0.0.1`[^nodeoct].

**`new RegExp(input)` and nested quantifiers like `(a+)*`.** One crafted string can take exponential time and block the event loop. Cap the input length and use the `re2` package for patterns users supply[^nodeloop].

**`eval`, `new Function` and `node:vm`.** `vm` is not a security mechanism[^nodevm]. Remote code execution through n8n's expression evaluation is on CISA's exploited list[^kev]. Run user code only in its own container. `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings` blocks `eval` and `new Function`[^nodecli].

**`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and user-supplied URLs.** React says raw HTML must come from a trusted source and be sanitized[^reactdom]. Accept only `https:` URLs, parsed with `new URL()`, and enforce Trusted Types with `require-trusted-types-for 'script'`[^mdntt].

blocks.title: Tools that catch it
items: **tsc.** `strict` plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, which `strict` omits[^tsconfig].

**typescript-eslint.** `strictTypeChecked` with `parserOptions.projectService: true` enables the `no-unsafe-*` rules, `no-implied-eval` and `no-non-null-assertion`. Add `no-unsafe-type-assertion` yourself[^tsestrict].
**CodeQL.** `js/command-line-injection`, `js/path-injection`, `js/request-forgery`, `js/prototype-polluting-assignment` and `js/polynomial-redos` cover TypeScript too[^cql].

**Node.js flags.** `--disable-proto=delete` removes `__proto__`[^nodecli] but not `constructor.prototype`[^owasppp]. `--permission` with `--allow-fs-read` limits what your code reads through `node:fs`[^nodeperm].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Hand-written type guards for request bodies.** They drift from the types they guard. Derive types from the schema with `z.infer`.
**eslint-plugin-security as your main check.** Its README warns of many false positives[^eslintsec]. Triage typed lint and CodeQL findings first.
**Freezing built-in prototypes.** `--frozen-intrinsics` is experimental[^nodecli] and freezing can break libraries[^owasppp]. Fix the merges instead.
**Escaping shell arguments yourself.** Drop the shell instead.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **React Server Components had a second critical bug.** An unauthenticated remote code execution flaw, exploitable only in rare cases, was fixed on 14 October in 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 and 19.3.1[^rscoct].

**Next.js shipped more middleware bypasses and critical fixes.** Five middleware or proxy bypasses came in May and July, and five critical remote code execution fixes from August to October[^nextadv]. Run at least 16.4.1 or 15.5.28[^nextsvg].
**TypeScript turned `strict` on by default.** TypeScript 6.0 did so in March[^ts6]. TypeScript 7.0, the native compiler, has no API until 7.1, so typescript-eslint needs TypeScript 6 alongside[^ts7].
**Node.js 20 reached end of life on 30 April.** Node.js 26 has been Active LTS since 28 October, and 22 ends on 30 April 2027[^noderel].
**Trusted Types work in every major browser.** They became Baseline in February[^mdntt], and React passes `TrustedHTML` to the DOM unchanged[^reactdom].

blocks.title: What this looks like for your code

columns.title: New project
items: Start on Node.js 26 with `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `strictTypeChecked` as errors.
Write one schema per input and derive the types from it.
In Next.js, keep data access and secrets in a `server-only` layer that authorizes[^nextsec].

columns.title: Existing codebase
items: Turn on the `no-unsafe-*` rules as warnings and fix request handlers first.
Search for `exec(`, `shell: true`, `eval(`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and `as any`.
Check authorization in handlers, not only middleware, and leave Node.js 20.

columns.title: High-assurance or regulated
items: Make CodeQL's `security-extended` suite a required check; private code needs a paid GitHub Code Security license[^codeqlcli].
Run services with `--permission`, `--disable-proto=delete` and minimal `--allow-*` grants.
Pen-test `proxy.ts` and route handlers regularly, as Next.js advises[^nextsec].
